newsitem.title: UK: OPEC output dips to 26.95 mln bpd in May - survey.
newsitem.headline: OPEC output dips to 26.95 mln bpd in May - survey.

text.p: OPEC output fell in May for the first time in 12 months, helping reverse sliding oil prices, but regular maintenance work at fields in the Gulf, rather than production restraint, was to blame.

Wellhead crude oil production from the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) fell by 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.95 million in May, a survey by Reuters of OPEC officials, oil companies and analysts found.

Nevertheless, the 11 OPEC countries still pumped more than 1.9 million bpd above their production ceiling of 25.03 million bpd, which is expected to be renewed for another six months at their Vienna ministerial meeting in three weeks time.
"If Brent holds in the $18-20 (a barrel) range nobody's going to be terribly disturbed by the level of OPEC production," said one member country official.
Benchmark Brent crude was trading at $18.46 a barrel on Thursday on London's International Petroleum Exchange.
Seasoned quota-busters Venezuela and Nigeria pushed production to the limit last month, halving overall OPEC losses in May and keeping the cartel's growth trend intact.
"There have been major increases in Venezuela and Nigeria. If you're looking for extra supply, that will do for me," said Geoff Pyne, oil analyst at UBS.

Iran's oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said recently last month's rally in Brent crude prices to a high of $20.60 reflected a new sense of quota discipline instilled during an informal gathering in the ancient Persian city of Isfahan.
But OPEC monitors said significant falls were restricted to the core Gulf states of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the only members keeping capacity in mothballs.
Lower Zakum and Umm Shaif field maintenance cut UAE output by 130,000 bpd to 2.12 million bpd, 40,000 bpd below quota.
Scheduled repairs also trimmed flows from the Neutral Zone shared by Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, taking their respective totals down 20,000 bpd to 8.08 million and 2.07 million bpd.

Iranian output was steady at 3.71 million bpd but Iraqi production slipped 10,000 bpd to 1.31 million bpd as the first $2 billion worth of exports under the United Nations oil-for-food deal were completed ahead of time.
The U.N. Security Council on Tuesday agreed to extend the pact for another 180 days starting on Saturday but Iraq has wound down production and is unlikely to resume exports until later in the month.
"They have scaled back production because their storage tanks are pretty full. We're not expecting the first cargo to load until about June 20," said one of Baghdad's customers.

OPEC's key Gulf trio of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the UAE were left looking increasingly isolated as the cartel's sole representatives in sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America both lifted production by 40,000 bpd in May.
Nigeria's output rose to 2.18 million bpd as Shell enjoyed a relatively trouble-free month after communal protests disrupted operations in March and April.
Venezuelan production rose to 3.2 million bpd also thanks to increased pumping rates at oilfields operated by foreign companies.
The Reuter survey seeks a best estimate of wellhead flows in OPEC countries based on the views of officials, industry monitors and analysts inside and outside member countries.
OPEC quotas are based on supply to market, defined to exclude movements to, but not sales from storage.
